# The bridge

`connect()` is the whole entry point: it waits for igni's hello, applies the theme and hands the page its bridge.

Read from the source: every name below, its signature, its JSDoc, and — for a type or a class — its own members.

| Name | Kind | Defined in | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`connect`](#connect) | function | `bridge.ts` | Wait for the host's `hello`, then hand back the bridge. |

## connect

```typescript
function connect<P extends LaunchParams = LaunchParams, S extends ExtensionSettings = ExtensionSettings,>(options: { timeoutMs?: number } = {}): Promise<Bridge<P, S>>
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `options` | `{ timeoutMs?: number }` | `{}` | how long to wait for the host's `hello` before giving up: `timeoutMs`, in milliseconds, and thirty seconds by default. |

Wait for the host's `hello`, then hand back the bridge.

Connecting is asynchronous because the host issues the nonce, and
without one there is nothing to say. An extension that renders
before awaiting this is rendering before it knows which extension
it is.

`P` and `S` name the extension's own launch parameters and settings;
the bridge passes on what the host sent without checking it against
them.

**Also** [`LaunchParams`](/docs/sdk/extension-bridge/reference-the-wire#launchparams), [`ExtensionSettings`](/docs/sdk/extension-bridge/reference-the-wire#extensionsettings), [`Bridge`](/docs/sdk/extension-bridge/reference-what-a-page-is-handed#bridge).
